message:
orderfile: on macOS, ask the process itself which signals it ignores (#43820)

### What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #43784 (its last review nit, which landed after the merge):
on macOS a `bun run orderfile` / `hints.ts` run that was started
ignoring SIGHUP or SIGINT (under `nohup`, as a background job of a
non-interactive script) died on that signal, because `withScratch` held
every ending signal there; only linux read which ones were being ignored
(`SigIgn` in `/proc/self/status`).

A child process cannot answer the question — Bun's spawn resets signal
dispositions in the children it starts — so the process asks about
itself: on macOS `sigaction(signal, NULL, &current)` through `bun:ffi`,
once, before `withScratch` adds any listener of its own. Signals whose
handler is `SIG_IGN` are left alone. When the call cannot be made (node,
a libc that will not open) every ending signal is held, as before. Linux
is unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- The same FFI call against glibc agrees with `/proc`'s `SigIgn` for a
process started under `trap "" HUP INT` and for one ignoring nothing
(new test, linux-glibc only).
- The nohup test runs on macOS again (it was linux-only); not run on
macOS locally — CI's darwin lanes are the check.
- `test/js/bun/perf/linker-order.test.ts` passes with gcc and clang;
`generate.ts` still loads under node (where the helper returns
`undefined`); end-to-end generator run: 191 of 191 app runs.
